replies.text: Peope like you make me sick. You point your little fingers, but you don't make any mention of anything that either of us did to perpetuate the rampant corruption. It must be the US's and the UK's fault. How can it possibly be anything else? I can't wait  to hear this, but how exactly are the US or the UK responsible for any of this? For that matter, how is ANYONE else responsible for Burundi's problems? If you're talking about that time after WW1 when Germany was sent packing and temporary Belgian oversight was established, then ok, I guess, but that's a pretty screwed up way of looking at it. Blaming someone else's help on the political corruption that has existed at the hands of Burundi's own leaders for six decades doesn't really make any sense. Is it maybe because the US and UK don't invest trillions of dollars dragging Burundi kicking and screaming forward into the 19th century and establishing infrastructure in a country that we all know the leaders of which will find a way to make themselves even more wealthy and then dismantle it and watch the whole thing burn? Is any Western country responsible for any of their coups? No. Did any Western nation ignite the civil wars that lasted there for many years? No. Is any western nation responsible in any way for the mass genocides that have occured there? No. That political corruption didn't happen until Burundi was on its own, a free nation, with its own constitution, and under no one else's rule but their own. Is that what you REALLY meant to say, that Burundi's leaders and the infighting between the Tutsis and the Hutus are the ones responsible for Burundi's poverty and almost zero infrastructure? What has Burundi done for itself in its 60+ years of independence besides fight with each other, overthrow each other's governments, commit mass genicide, and assassinate each other's leaders? You'll have to excuse me for being more than a little bit critical of sending aid to Burundi, but I think we all understand that if that happened, their leaders would only find a way to exploit it and none of that help would ever trickle down to the people, so why bother? Everything I've ever known about Burundi indicates that neither the US nor the UK are responsible in any way for Burundi's problems. Neither of us have done anything, at any point in history, to keep that country impoverished and in constant conflict with itself. It seems to me that every time we try to establish a fair form of government anywhere to try to help the people, as soon as we leave, it all falls apart. Maybe what Burundi really needs back is some form of Colonialism, because they sure as Hell aren't capable of running their own country.
